recipes.name: Pan-Seared Lemon Tilapia with Parmesan Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch salt and ground black pepper
1 pinch salt and ground black pepper

steps.text: Start the pasta: Bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a boil over medium heat. Stir in macaroni and return to a boil. Cook, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes.

While the pasta is cooking, make the fish: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sprinkle tilapia on both sides with lemon juice, oregano, basil, cilantro, salt, and pepper. Place fillets into the hot skillet making sure they don't touch. Sear until golden brown on the outside and opaque and flaky on the inside, 2 to 4 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.

Finish the pasta: Drain the macaroni and return to the saucepan. Add olive oil and stir to coat. Mix in Parmesan cheese, then mix in lemon juice, garlic powder, basil, oregano, cilantro, salt, and pepper.
Divide pasta between two plates and top each with a tilapia fillet.

raw_recipe.headline: Pan-Seared Lemon Tilapia with Parmesan Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Not all fish pasta recipes are as tasty as this one! Tender tilapia seasoned with lemon and herbs is served over Parmesan pasta for a light, fresh taste.

review.reviewBody: My family ate everything on their plate. Loved it! I baked the tilapia - 375 degrees for 12 minutes. I cooked for 4 people so for the pasta, I used 10 ounces of pasta, 2 tsp. lemon juice, 1 cup parmesean, 1/4 tsp. each of oregano, basil, and cilantro. When I drained the pasta, I reserved some of the pasta water just in case I wanted to add it, and I'm glad I did. Once, I got all of the pasta, cheese, & herbs in the pan I decided that a little bit of the pasta water would give the pasta the exact consistency I was looking for. I did not measure how much I used, but it was probably about 1 Tbls maybe 2. I served this w/ broccoli as well. We will have this again!!!!

The pasta was delicious but the tilipia left something to be desired. Even though I more than doubled the seasonings, it was still bland. The seaoning is really important when cooking tilapia because it is such a mild fish. I would not make the fish again, but I will definitely make the pasta as a side with parmesan crusted tilapia (very easy to make: 1/2 C grated parm, 1 Tbsp garlic powder, 1 C panko crumbs, 1 tsp oregano, 1 egg, beaten: dip in egg wash, coat with combined dry ingredients and cook in heated light olive oil over meduim heat 4 min each side).

This turned out pretty well. Used lemon pepper with the basil, oregano and cilantro for the seasoning for the fish, but let it marinate for an hour or so in the fridge. Then with the parm sauce ingredients, I added heavy cream to get more of a sauce, simmered a bit before adding the fish. Minimal adjustments for a nice recipe, probably will do again.

Very, very good. Used a cast-iron skillet to sear the fish. Sauteed 3 (small) cloves of garlic in the olive oil for the pasta and mixed all the pasta ingredients together before adding to the cooked farfalle (bowtie) pasta (instead of macaroni), along with a pinch of lemon zest. Fast to make, easy, and great flavor.

The basis of this dish is really good. I'm eating very healthy right now so i baked mine with the seasonings and just a rub of olive oil on a bed of seasoned asparagus in foil and then made my pasta with white wheat low carb spaghetti noodles and olive oil. I cut the parm to 3 tbl spoons for about 6 oz pasta and added the herbs and seasonings and it was great. The flavor was there.

This recipe is SO good. My husband absolutely loved it. I didn't really follow measurements for the spices. I eyed what I wanted. I also baked the tilapia at 375 degrees until it was slightly brown on the edges and it worked out perfect! The pasta was great. I used different noodles than elbow. I used cellantini and added pasta water like a previous reviewer mentioned. It would also be great with Alfredo sauce. Next time I'm making extra!

Good, but definitely needs additional seasoning. A pinch of each spice is not enough. I more than doubled the spices in both the fish and the pasta. I also reduced the olive oil for the fish to 1 tbsp and that was plenty. You really need to crank up the heat to medium high to get any kind of crust on the fish. This made more than two servings (three adult servings for us), unless you have a huge appetite. Serve it with a vegetable or salad.

Baked, as per a previous reviewer, 375 for 12 minutes. The seasoning on the fish complimented it very well. The pasta itself was a little lemony, so I will probably cut the lemon juice next time for the pasta. Everything else was delicious! I used whole grain pasta, so this was a very WW friendly recipe!

Taste: I made without cilantro (I thought I had some and it had gone bad in the fridge). I added extra fresh basil to the pasta and just used half a lemon's juice on the tilapia and the other half in the pasta. Subtle basil/parmesan with a light fish and a heavy pasta with a side of asparagus tied with lemon: very delish. Didn't need extra pepper. Husband (who is picky about heavy foods) loved it. Not fishy at all.

Presentation: Beige on beige and the fish didn't brown well. Added extra fresh basil. and server steamed asparagus between pasta base and fish top to give it a pretty look.

Ease: My husband who, god bless his soul, has trouble with pancakes handled this very well. It's easy to season and taste as you go. Texture is easy to monitor and everything goes in 4 minute cycles so there's no timer overlap.

I made some adjustments. I hardly ever measure spices only less I'm baking. I did an even coat of lemon juice and seasoning on each side of the tilapia. Used fettuccine noodles, left some water in the pot when I was done cooking the noodles, 1 cup of Parmesan cheese, added a thin layer of garlic powder, few light squeezes of lemon juice, and nickle sized seasoning. Served with Corn, Carrot and Asparagus steamers. It was a hit!
Fish and pasta were very good! I did bake my fish rather than fry in a pan, and did not have, nor like cilantro. Will definitely make again!

This was a good flavored dish after I added more herbs, salt and pepper because tilapia is a bland flavored fish to begin with. I used the cast iron skillet and the seared part of the fish stuck, dont know why that happened. For the macaroni, I also used 6 cheese shredded italian cheese as well as the parm, because We like the mac more cheesy. Overall I rate this very good!
Great base recipe. I used farfalle pasta, added red pepper flakes and sautéed peas. It needed quite a bit more salt, garlic and pepper. But overall good and will make again
Very easy to make and very yummy!! Made it for my boyfriend, we loved it!! Yummmmm

I would suggest swapping the olive oil for butter. I do like tilapia, but keep in mind it’s a delicate fish, and will fall apart if you’re not careful with the preparation. I think snapper would also work.

This was a pretty good recipe. It was easy to follow. I felt it was a little lacking in flavor. We served it with sautéed veggies and that gave it a bit more flavor. Next time I make it, I will add some red pepper flakes to the pasta to give it a little heat.
Absolutely delicious

Flavor was good using the spices in the recipe, but was a little dry. May try it again, except next time with a butter and white wine sauce. The pasta also a little dry, possibly needs a little more Parmesan.
used trout and it was fine, penne instead of macaroni
Shashank- Talapia was cooked at perfection and elbow macaroni was the best pasta which goes with sea food. I love the texture that this recipe has.
